angle: WR/TE break mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G), matched to the same NFL route families (slant, out, hitch, in, corner) and tested against season separation over expected on held-out draft classes; positive use = a next-season shortlist rule for day-3 / undrafted receivers built on SOE, with Break G shown not to sort it.
metric_name: Break G: mean acceleration magnitude (g) over the 1.0 s centred on the sharpest point of the first route break, z-scored within drill x Combine year, averaged over route drills and reliability-shrunk; identical code on NFL snaps; rule frozen and hashed in frozen_rule.json
headline_number: Held-out slope -0.4 in of season SOE per sd of Break G (90% interval -2.2 to +1.7, n=116, ridge forecast as covariate, shuffle p=0.74; +3 in gain ruled out, p=0.0025). Shortlist rule (SOE > 0, 100+ routes) hits next season 62% (16/26) vs 19% (5/27) passed over, gap 43 pts [21, 63], Fisher p=0.002; day-3/UDFA pool 6/12 vs 2/8 (base 40%).
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of the round-12 winner (round_12/revised, 8.41). Football: the positive use is now the headline, a pre-specified shortlist rule (last-season SOE > 0, 100+ routes) scored on the unseen next season against a base rate and the passed-over group, with a day-3/UDFA subset, a soft-vs-hard-cut split inside the shortlist (Break G does not sort it), and a named 2026 list (13 names, shortlist_2026.csv); day 3 now defined by draft round 4+ instead of pick >= 100. The board is cut to the six Figure-1 receivers with deployment columns and role-specific actions, plus a drill-vs-tape disagreement case (Kayshon Boutte: hardest drill cutter, enters NFL breaks faster than the median and cuts at 0.48 g vs 0.62 in drills; coaching point given). Jargon (57/70-test ledger, Holm, shuffle, REML, jackknife) moved to the Appendix; results table is 5 rows. Data science: the main test uses a ridge (shrunken) forecast entered as a covariate so its held-out calibration is estimated (pooled weight 0.72) instead of assumed (round-12 slopes 0.40/0.64/1.33), with a class-stratified player bootstrap that refits forecast and penalty: -0.4 [-2.2, +1.7]. New target-quality adjustment: season SOE adjusted for route mix and depth at the throw from 1,902 random (non-EPA) sampled snaps: -1.1 [-2.7, +1.3]. New outcomes not dependent on separation: yards per route run +0.24 [0.03, 0.47] but +0.10 [-0.01, 0.25] without Nacua; catch rate over expected +1.8 pts but +0.1 without Nacua. Price lead tested held out (14% [5, 23], R2 8.3 -> 9.7, Holm 16%). Ledger extended to 70 tests. BLAS threads pinned to 1 (the QB REML step went from >13 min to 5 s on a shared 4-core box). Writeup: 1,785 words by check.py and 1,948 by wc -w (both < 2,000); lede simplified; 'Why receivers, why now', Combine-week protocol and the checks run-on removed or merged into action 3; motivation backed by the price evidence and SOE stability. Viz: Figure 1 is now the drill-vs-NFL cut cards (hero), readouts at 11 pt, purple/green legend beside the strips, g explained in the caption; the GM scatter is dropped; old Fig 4 (forest, cut to 8 rows) and Fig 5 (price vs value) merged into one figure, with Break G drawn twice (beyond position only, and beyond the athletic profile = the numbers in the text) to fix the 9% vs 14% mismatch, a shaded 'clubs pay, below the margin' region and the +3 in line; the per-class rows that poked past the margin are gone (per-class slopes quoted in text, all negative); chain caterpillar clipped at +/-60 in with arrows and the five largest slopes named; new shortlist figure with Wilson intervals.
open_risks: The headline remains a bounded null for Break G; losses down to -2.2 in per sd are not excluded

The shortlist evidence comes mainly from the all-rounds pool (53 pairs, 38 receivers, some counted twice); the day-3/UDFA pool alone (20 pairs) is not significant (gap 25 pts [-14, 58], Fisher p=0.26), and the rule is about SOE persistence, not Combine tracking
Over all 70 ledger tests, Bonferroni would leave nothing below 5%, the shortlist included (raw p=0.002)

Not a blind test: earlier rounds saw all three classes; the switch to a ridge-as-covariate main test was made this round, after the plain-forecast result was known (the plain version, -1.2 [-3.5, +1.0], is still shown)
Yards per route run and catch-over-expected leads depend on Puka Nacua
Board actions are football judgement from deployment shares; the Boutte coaching point rests on 7 graded NFL breaks
Game tracking is a 40-play sample per player, half selected for high EPA; the route-mix adjustment uses only the random half
